neighbours.label: words naming the person or role that work is done for, in hiring and employment contexts (hired to care for his niece, employed him as her steward)
fire: A young nanny is hired by a widower to care for his two children.
The duchess took him into her house and employed him as her steward.
Recruiters struggle to find candidates who fit what they are looking for.
Your skills are exactly what many charities could use right now.
She found work cleaning in the homes of wealthy families in the city.
The firm hired a driver to take its clients to the airport.
He was employed by the farmer to tend his sheep through the winter.
The agency places tutors with families who need help at home.
quiet: A young nanny moved to a new town with her two children.
The duchess lived alone in her house near the old steward's cottage.
The hikers struggled to find the path they had walked before.
Your skills will improve a lot with steady practice right now.
She grew up in one of the wealthy homes in the city.
The firm moved its offices closer to the airport.
The farmer kept his sheep in the barn through the winter.
The families gathered at the school to talk about the new term.

notes: Top examples are hiring/job contexts (skill set many nonprofits could use; hired to care for his niece; what they are looking for; employed him as her steward; cleaning in the homes of the well-off). Near misses keep the nouns without the employment frame.
